content: Breast milk may contain this medication, which could potentially cause harmful effects on a nursing infant. Therefore, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this drug. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. It is important to maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Combining this medication with monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors can result in a severe, potentially fatal drug interaction. Avoid using MAO inhibitors (e.g., isocarboxazid, linezolid, methylene blue, phenelzine, selegiline, tranylcypromine) during treatment with this medication. Most MAO inhibitors should also not be taken for two weeks before starting this medication. Caffeine can amplify the side effects of this medication. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Notes: Do not share this medication with others. Appetite suppressants should not replace a proper diet. If it is near the time of your next dose or late in the evening, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Side Effects: Common side effects may include dizziness, dry mouth, difficulty sleeping, irritability, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation. Rarely, it can cause serious, potentially fatal lung or heart problems (e.g., pulmonary hypertension, heart valve issues), especially with prolonged use or when combined with other appetite suppressants. Severe allergic reactions are rare. If you experience any concerning symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Precautions: Before taking benzphetamine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other sympathomimetic amines (e.g., pseudoephedrine, amphetamine, phentermine), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness, and alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. If you have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly and share the results with your doctor. Benzphetamine must not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm an unborn baby. If you become pregnant or suspect you are pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. Infants born to mothers who have used this medication for a prolonged period or in high doses may experience withdrawal symptoms, such as irritability or extreme fatigue. Breastfeeding: This drug may pass into breast milk and could harm a nursing infant. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication.
